data.title: Segmented
data.tagline: Switch quickly between a few short, exclusive modes
data.description: A segmented control keeps several short options visible together. It often changes a view, sort order, or time range and usually does not navigate to a new page. If options are numerous or their labels are long, choose another control.

distinctions.label: Button / button group
distinctions.explanation: Segmented contains mutually exclusive choices: selecting one clears another. A Button or button group runs actions and does not imply exclusive options.

use: A few mutually exclusive display modes
avoid: Use it for many long choices
Treat it as primary page navigation
Use icons whose meaning is not obvious
Use it as an on-off setting; choose a Switch

lessonPractice.title: A file toolbar needs an immediate choice between List view and Grid view. What control fits best?

options.label: Use a two-part segmented control that keeps the current view highlighted
options.feedback: The choices are short, mutually exclusive display modes for the same content, which fits a segmented control.

options.label: Use tabs and treat the views as two content pages
options.feedback: There are no separate content sections here; only the presentation of the same files changes.

options.label: Use one switch where on and off stand for the two views
options.feedback: List and Grid are named peer modes, not the enabled and disabled states of one setting.

data.agentPrompt: Add a List/Grid segmented control to the file toolbar. Change only how the same files are displayed, keep the current mode highlighted, and test keyboard use and the default after refresh.
